lessons.title: From peach baskets to the shot clock
lessons.objective: Place Naismith, the BAA/NBA merger and the 24-second clock.

payload.prompt: Put basketball history milestones in order.

items.text: BAA founded as pro basketball league
BAA and NBL merge to form the NBA

explanation.correct: Perfect. Basketball grew from a YMCA winter exercise in 1891 to a pro league in 1946, the NBA in 1949 and the shot clock in 1954.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. The order is Naismith in 1891, the BAA in 1946, the BAA and NBL merger that made the NBA in 1949, then the 24-second clock in 1954.

payload.prompt: Why did Naismith invent basketball?

options.text: To give athletes an indoor sport for winter.
To replace football as America's favorite sport.
To create a game for professional players.

explanation.correct: Right. In 1891 Naismith needed something his students could play indoors between football and baseball seasons, and peach baskets did the job.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Basketball started as a practical winter sport, not as pro entertainment.

payload.prompt: What did the NBA start as?

options.text: The BAA, founded 1946 and merged with the NBL in 1949.
A direct spinoff of college basketball.
A league that started in 1954.

explanation.correct: Exactly. The BAA became the NBA after absorbing the NBL.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. NBA history: BAA 1946, merger 1949, then growth from there.

payload.prompt: Fill in the shot clock story.
payload.template: The NBA added a {{seconds}}-second shot clock in {{year}}, because teams with a lead used to {{problem}} the ball.

explanation.correct: Right. Before the clock, a team ahead could just hold the ball. Games turned into slow, low-scoring stalls, and the 24-second clock brought the scoring and the fans back.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. The NBA introduced a 24-second clock for the 1954-55 season because teams with a lead were stalling, which made games slow and dull.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: Basketball is actually pretty young as a sport.

payload.question: What is she noting?

options.text: Basketball is just over 130 years old, younger than baseball or football.
Basketball players are younger than football players.
The game changes every season.
Most players retire young.

payload.translation: She means basketball started in 1891, making it newer than baseball and football.

followUps.line: That explains why the game changed so much.
followUps.why: Good recognition that younger sports evolve faster than established ones.

followUps.line: American game, basically.
followUps.why: Fair observation that Naismith's invention became an American institution.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Basketball is genuinely young: Naismith invented it in 1891. Baseball and football started earlier.

explanation.incorrect: Bill Russell won 11 championships in 13 seasons with the Celtics (1957-1969), the most of any player ever. Defense and teamwork were the engine.

explanation.incorrect: Not quite. The 1960s featured dominant centers like Wilt and Russell at the peak.

lessons.title: Jordan, the Dream Team and going global
lessons.objective: Explain the Bulls dynasty and the 1992 Olympic team.

payload.prompt: Fill in Jordan's Bulls run.
payload.template: Jordan's Bulls won {{titles}} championships in two three-peats: 1991 to 1993 and {{years}}.

explanation.correct: Right. Six titles in two three-peats, with a break in between while Jordan tried baseball and then returned in 1995.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. The Bulls won six titles: 1991 to 1993, then 1996 to 1998, after Jordan's break from basketball.

payload.prompt: What was special about the 1992 Dream Team?

options.text: NBA stars like Jordan, Magic and Bird played in the Olympics for the first time and won easily.
It was a team of high school players.
It lost a game in the Olympics.

explanation.correct: Exactly. Until then the US sent college players. In 1992 NBA pros were allowed for the first time, and the Dream Team won gold by huge margins.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. The 1992 Dream Team was the first US Olympic team with NBA stars, and it won gold by huge margins.

payload.prompt: How did the Dream Team change basketball?

options.text: It made the NBA a worldwide brand, and more international players followed.
It invented three-pointers.
It changed the rules of basketball.

explanation.correct: Right. The Dream Team sparked huge interest abroad, and over the next decades more international players reached the NBA.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. The Dream Team did not change the rules or invent the three. It showed NBA-level basketball to the world and inspired a generation of international players.

Jordan lost his first Finals and won the rest.

Jordan only played in the Finals once.

payload.translation: She means the Bulls reached the Finals six times with Jordan and won all six, which is why fans call his record perfect.

followUps.line: Wasn't there a gap in the middle for baseball?
followUps.why: A fair, curious question: Jordan left in 1993, tried baseball and returned in 1995.

followUps.line: Six for six is wild.
followUps.why: A warm, honest reaction that shows you get why the record stands out.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Jordan was also Finals MVP all six times. Ask her which Finals she remembers best.

followUps.line: Other countries caught up fast, though.
followUps.why: Fair: within a couple of decades international teams were competing with the US.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Dream Team (1992) is widely credited with globalizing basketball and inspiring international talent pipelines.

lessons.title: Shaq, Kobe, Duncan and LeBron

lessons.title: Curry, the Warriors and the three
lessons.objective: Explain how the Warriors changed shot selection.

payload.prompt: What was the Curry-era Warriors dynasty?

options.text: Five straight Finals from 2015 to 2019, with titles in 2015, 2017 and 2018.
A title in every year of the 1990s.
A single title in 1975 and nothing since.

explanation.correct: Right. Curry, Thompson and Green won in 2015, Durant joined in 2016 and they won again in 2017 and 2018. They added another title in 2022.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. The Warriors reached five straight Finals from 2015 to 2019 and won in 2015, 2017 and 2018, then again in 2022.

payload.prompt: What is small-ball basketball?

options.text: Putting shooters at every position instead of traditional big men.
Using a smaller basketball.
Playing with fewer than five players.

explanation.correct: Exactly. The Warriors' famous lineup played Draymond Green, a 6-foot-6 forward, at center with four shooters around him.
explanation.incorrect: Not quite. Small-ball means replacing a traditional big with another shooter or wing to spread the floor, like the Warriors did with Draymond Green at center.

payload.prompt: The NBA had a three-point line before Curry arrived. Right?

scene.alt: A timeline showing the NBA three-point line adopted in 1979-80 and Curry's Warriors winning in 2015.

explanation.correct: Right. The NBA adopted the three-point line in 1979-80. The revolution was a slow change in how teams used it, and Curry's Warriors pushed it to the extreme.
explanation.incorrect: The NBA adopted the three-point line in 1979-80, decades before Curry. What changed in the 2010s was how much teams used it, and Curry's Warriors showed how far that could go.
explanation.sayThisLine: "The line has been there since 1979. Curry just made teams use it."

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: Curry changed how defenses had to cover the three-point line.

payload.question: What is she describing?

options.text: Curry's range forced defenses to extend further, creating more space for others.
Curry invented the three-pointer.
Curry moved the three-point line.
Curry only shoots threes.

payload.translation: She means Curry could shoot from so far beyond the arc that defenders had to pick him up far from the basket.

followUps.line: That opened up cuts and drives for everyone else.
followUps.why: Exactly: Curry's threat created opportunities for teammates.

followUps.line: Copy-cat effect around the league.
followUps.why: True: other teams drafted shooters to compete.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Curry's range forced defenses to stretch out, and that opened the floor for cuts and drives.

statement.speaker: Your crush
statement.text: Small-ball works because everyone can guard everyone.

payload.question: What does she mean?

options.text: Without traditional big men, all five players can switch defensively.
No one plays defense in small-ball.
Shorter players are harder to guard.
Small-ball only works on small courts.

payload.translation: She's noting that small-ball's switchability gives defensive flexibility.

followUps.line: But you lose rebounding.
followUps.why: Valid tradeoff: small-ball sacrifices size for perimeter defense.

followUps.line: Works if everyone can shoot.
followUps.why: Exactly: small-ball requires spacing and shooting ability.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Small-ball works through switchability: all five can guard positions 1-5.

payload.prompt: What share of NBA shots are threes these days?

explanation.correct: Right. Around four in ten NBA shots are threes in recent seasons, up from under one in ten around 1990.
explanation.incorrect: Recent NBA seasons have seen roughly 40% of shots taken from three, up from under 10% around 1990. That jump is what people mean by the three-point revolution.

lessons.title: AAU, one-and-done and hoop culture

payload.prompt: Fill in the college-to-NBA shortcut.

payload.prompt: What does sneaker and tunnel culture mean?
